cell.label: Patient with resolved stone episode. Previous episode?
Conservative management: increase urine output to 2.1 qt (2 L) per day. Consider lower sodium intake. Consider lower meat intake (all types)
Obtain history: number of previous episodes, onset of previous episodes, bowel disease, gout, diabetes, medications, family history
Serum studies 24-hour urine studies. Uncomplicated calcium stone disease (ie, normocalcemia, no bowel disease, no UTI)?
Add potassium chloride if patient has normal urine citrate levels. Add potassium citrate if patient has low urine citrate levels
Prescribe tiopronin (Thiola) and increase fluid intake
Add acetohydroxamic acid (Lithostat) for severe infection stones

footnotes.footnote: Most patients treated with thiazides will require potassium citrate.
From Pietrow PK, Karellas ME. Medical management of common urinary calculi. Am Fam Physician 2006;74:86-94.
*The American Urological Association does not recommend allopurinol as first-line treatment
